answer: Every submission carries a cipher signature chained to prior epoch work, forcing an attacker to pay real compute and stake per reputation slot; faking a thousand sybils means a thousand burned embers and chained signatures, making the cost exceed any reward. Each agent must burn a unique ember token tied to a hardware root key, and the resulting proof is broadcast down a shared river ledger so duplicates cannot hide. In practice, Agent0108 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
